questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I could get classes taught in English

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. My receiving university had a informative homepage and people

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information about the university and classes that helped me to know my way around and which modules to choose

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There was several accommodations to chose from both with same sex and mixed flats, rooms with shared or individual bathrooms and so on

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
All accommodations had cooking facilities but the ones that weren´t catered had better and bigger facilities.
I lived in a non-catered accommodation and was very satisfied with the facilities, though I had to buy pots, pans, knifes and everything else to cook with myself since nothing besides a plate, bowl, glass, mug and cutlery was there. But my flatmates were really kind to let me use some of their kitchen inventory so I did not have to buy that many things

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you´re only on exchange for one semester you aren´t securred a on campus housing so make sure to search for something else well before your exchange, but besides that most of on campus housing is close to the city center and the main campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have their own online homepage for exchange students where it is listed the steps you have to go through to apply. I had to fill out personal information and upload the acceptance letter to go abroad from University of Copenhagen. Thereafter I had to write an essay about why I wanted to go on exchange and why I wanted to go to Newcastle. When they approved me I had to read some information and check that I had read and understood/accepted the things and then i received information on how to proper registrate at their university and make my own account to be in their system. Everything was quite simple and easy to do and it did not take to long.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The homepage had help in itself and I could e-mail several different people depending on what I needed help with and if it was the wrong one they would forward the e-mail. It was also possible to call them if urgent, but I didn´t have the need to do that

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. It was an easy process

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the steps shown and do it within the timeframe

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is hard to compare excactly since it was a different law system and a different way to learn law, but in general the level was more or less the same though it took some time to get used to the way the classes are tought but the content wasn´t to complicated.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There was a lot more lectures than seminars so a lot more one-way learning rather than the seminars we are used to. Also there was no group work to prepare, you did most of the preparing by your self and talked about at the seminars. 
There was also some selfstudying to do. You had to read some texts but you could often chose what to read yourself since it is more based on theories and cases so you just need to find something that covers all of it and the teachers do give you a reading list to chose from.
Every class was also only one hour so I did not have as many classes as at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Employment Law
Law and Literature
Law and Gender

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed employment law and find it very interesting especially because it gives a good perspective on the employment laws in the UK and I was able to compare it to what I knew from back home and see how different it is.
Law and gender was a very interesting and different module to have that gave several tools and perspectives on this area.
Law and literature was a subject I would recommend but it can be a bit bored if you don´t have anyone you know who takes the same module. It is a bit more fun if you have someone to take it with.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The train tickets varied a lot in price and could be a bit expensive at times

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything and if you really couldn´t find anything in your interest you could start a new society/club

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did zumba with a few people I had meet which was really fun  and a fun workout along with some socials

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Walk around in the city and get to know it or travel to bigger cities. Newcastle is pretty nice centered so it is possible to take the train to a lot of places like Edinburgh, London, York and so on and be there within two/two and half hours

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, the local culture is quite similar though there are differences that are interesting to try and hear about

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say yes to everything you can in the beginning and sign up for a society or two, and don´t be scarred to walk over and say hi to new people. The changes are that they are just as interested in meeting you and other new people as you yourself are

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really find any cultural differences challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved how open and kind everyone was, They were always ready to help

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look and apply for accomodation in good time before you leave for exchange, join a society or a club and keep an open mind and remember to have fun

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I was able to live on my own in another country and the people I met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To fully understand how the city and country worked in the beginning and to adjust to the teaching methods

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
